was: Oceanfront RV park & marina on Johnstone Strait, north Vancouver Island; 100+ serviced and unserviced RV/tent sites, accommodates big rigs; washrooms, showers, laundry, camp store, boat/kayak launch. Reservable via Campspot. Open ~mid-May to end of Sep. --Claude
note: Private RV park and marina near Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, on 30 acres of private land with abundant walk-on waterfront, run by the McGrady and Brockway families.  Its more than 80 sites run from tent sites to big rigs: fully serviced pull-throughs, full-service 15- or 30-amp sites (some with an ocean view), rustic oceanfront tent sites and The Mecca's four non-serviced group sites.  There is a two-lane launch ramp usable at all tides, a 43-slip marina for boats up to 26 ft, an easy kayak launch and a fish-cleaning station, plus a Level 2 car charger and propane fills up to 100 lb, and Roxy's Diner, a licensed food truck with an ocean-view patio, serves burgers and local lingcod fish and chips.  Partner operators run fishing, bear-viewing and whale-watching tours.  Generators may run from 9 to 11 a.m. and 6 to 8 p.m.  The resort also has long-term RV sites, park-model cottages and two RV trailer rentals, and a residential phase, Orca Views, is coming. --Claude

was: Newer forested RV resort at 1066 Gilmour Road, Gibsons (Sunshine Coast), ~9 min from Langdale ferry and at the Sprockids Park trailhead. 34 sites total (3 tent-only), max RV length 50 ft, full/electric/water hookups, laundry. Transient nightly camping reservable via Campspot. --Claude
note: Newly built campground in a quiet forest setting, nestled against expansive public rainforest in Gibsons on the Sunshine Coast, 5 minutes from the Langdale ferry, beaches and the town centre, with direct access to the Sprockids Mountain Bike Park, Mount Elphinstone and the rainforest trail network.  Most sites have a fire pit, and there are large group sites for events of 100 or more people, and lodges.  Quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. --Claude

was: New (opened 2025) 22-site RV park on the east side of Hwy 23 about 1 km north of Halcyon Hot Springs, ~25 min from Nakusp above Upper Arrow Lake. Paved roads, 20-50-amp power, rinse-water taps, washrooms/showers, dump station, firepits/picnic tables, camp store, free WiFi; group sites available. Transient nightly camping reservable via Campspot. --Claude
note: Campground overlooking Upper Arrow Lake in the heart of the Kootenays, 25 minutes from Nakusp and an hour from Revelstoke; Halcyon Resort's hot-spring pools, spa and dining are 1 km away.  Every site has a lake view except site 4, which looks onto the forest, and sites 23 and 24 are creekside.  Water is at every site, and drinking water and ice are sold at the camp store.  There is a playground, a nature walking trail with cougar and bear exhibits, private waterfalls, a horseshoe pit and cornhole, mountain-bike and e-bike rentals, and backcountry access to biking, ATV and walking trails.  Generators may run at non-electric sites from 9 to 11 a.m. and 4 to 7 p.m., and the person booking must be at least 19.  A lakeview cottage and suite are rented all year. --Claude

was: 154 sites (45 pull-through, 115 full hookup 30/50amp) beside the St. Mary River near Kimberley; heated pool, 18-hole mini-golf, store, laundry, dump station. Nightly reservable via Campspot; open Apr 15-Oct 15. --Claude
note: Campground beside the St. Mary's River, an 8-minute drive south-west of Kimberley's town centre, the Platzl, with over 150 campsites.  Full-service sites 26-67 and 91-140, in the Mountain View and Pine Meadows areas, take 15- to 50-amp power and rigs of 25 to 45 ft, and the riverview sites 68-79 take 30 or 50 amps and 25 to 35 ft; sites 26, 27, 28, 39, 41, 43, 45, 47, 49, 53-57 and 110-140 are pull-throughs.  The power-and-water back-ins, 1 to 25B (15 or 30 amps, 25 to 40 ft), are closest to the pool and mini-golf, and the non-service sites NS1 to NS9 (20 to 25 ft) are first come, first served.  A free heated pool is open from mid-May to the September long weekend and an 18-hole putting course from early May to late September, and there is a timber picnic shelter, a playground, bocce, horseshoes and sand volleyball.  The Adventure Centre rents e-bikes, stand-up paddleboards and inflatable kayaks and sells Kootenay Rafting Company tours.  Cell service is spotty.  In winter the bathrooms behind the office stay open with running water and hot showers, tanks are filled there from a hose, and the sani-dump is at site 26.  Winter storage costs C$250 from October 1 to April 20.  The campground also rents trailers and trapper's tents and has walk-in tent sites. --Claude

season.note: Full services from April 15 to October 15.  From October 15 to April 15, select sites at the top of the campground stay open, by reservation, with 15- and 30-amp power but no water or sewer hookups.

was: Pathfinder-operated concession campground in Metro Vancouver's Brae Island Regional Park on the Fraser River at Fort Langley (9451 Glover Rd). 156 RV sites with 30-amp and 30/50-amp full hookups plus 5 tent-cabins and a group tent area; drive-in, ~$51-73/night, 2-night minimum, 30-night max stay (transient), recreational season mid-April to mid-October plus a winter RV program. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights on every RV site (Campspot, October 2026 and July 2027 weeknights, 2026-10-12). --Claude
note: Campground in Metro Vancouver's Brae Island Regional Park, beside the Fraser River at Fort Langley and within walking distance of the historic village; Pathfinder Camp Resorts runs it under licence from Metro Vancouver.  All of its RV sites have 30-amp power and water, and some have 30/50-amp full hookups for self-contained RVs; there is also a group tent area for 65 people (up to 100) and five tent cabins.  The camp store and BERG bike rentals open from Canada Day to Labour Day, propane is sold, and summer weekends are themed.  The campground is gated around the clock, with gate entry cards; showers cost C$2 for 10 minutes, and mosquitoes can be a nuisance when the river runs high. --Claude

season.note: Recreational camping from April to October; a recreational winter RV program runs from October to April.

was: Oceanfront RV resort & marina on Pedder Bay near Metchosin/Victoria, southern Vancouver Island. Full-hookup back-in and pull-through sites (30/50 amp, water, sewer, cable, WiFi), big-rig friendly, some oceanfront; general store, cafe, 3-lane boat launch, moorage. Nightly bookable via Campspot. --Claude
note: Oak Bay Marine Group resort and marina on Pedder Bay, 40 minutes from downtown Victoria, against a backdrop of the Olympic Mountain Range and the Race Rocks Ecological Reserve.  Its fully serviced RV sites are oceanfront, back-in or pull-through, with 30-amp, double 30-amp or 50-amp power, and a seasonal dry-camping area opens from spring to fall, where generators may run from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.  The marina has a fuel dock, a boat-launch ramp, moorage for vessels of 18 to 56 ft, boat and kayak rentals and guided fishing charters.  There is a coffee house and licensed snack bar, an off-leash dog park, and bunkies to rent. --Claude

was: Oceanfront RV resort & marina on the Strait of Georgia south of Campbell River, Vancouver Island. 155 full-service RV sites (30/50 amp, water, sewer, propane, dump), ranging from beachfront sites on the ocean to treed sites among Douglas firs; general store, pool, marina, boat launch, fuel. Cabins also available. Nightly bookable via Campspot. --Claude
note: Resort and marina near Campbell River on the Georgia Strait.  Its Front Row big-rig sites, 16 to 30 ft wide and 60 to 80 ft deep under Douglas firs, overlook the marina, the Georgia Strait and the Coast Mountain Range, and at peak times they need a rig of 25 to 30 ft or more.  Rows A and B, under the trees, are 38 to 45 ft deep; the Main Park has treed sites about 18 ft wide and 46 ft deep, and sunny ones.  The Lighthouse beachfront sites have no trees and a fire pit on a raised seaside berm, and the Lighthouse non-beachfront sites have 50-amp power, many backing onto a nature conservation area.  A heated pool and a hot tub (16 and over) open from mid-May to mid-September; there is an adult rec hall and clubhouse with a stone fireplace, beach volleyball, horseshoes, shuffleboard and swing golf, a seasonal Sugar Shack, a community fire pit and the Oyster River nature trail.  The boat ramp costs C$15 a launch, and there is moorage.  Cottages and park models are also rented. --Claude

was: Private resort at 988 Spahats Creek Forest Service Rd near Spahats Falls on the Clearwater Valley (Trophy Mountain) road, gateway to Wells Gray; 45 sites - serviced (30-amp power, water), unserviced and group campsites plus cabins. Washrooms with toilets/showers, dump station, laundry, internet. Transient/nightly, reservable online via Campspot. Open May 1-Oct 31. --Claude
note: Resort across from the Spahats Falls day-use area at the gateway to Wells Gray Provincial Park, between Kamloops and Jasper, near the Trophy Mountain flower meadows and Helmcken Falls.  It has private forested sites and easy pull-in, pull-out sites, serviced (30-amp power, water and internet) or unserviced, plus group sites, and commercial and work-camp sites with a full-size gymnasium and a helicopter landing area.  There is an outdoor dish sink, sites have picnic tables and fire pits, and firewood is sold.  For swimming, the resort recommends Dutch Lake, 15 minutes away.  Three 1,700 sq ft four-bedroom cottages are also rented, and the minimum stay varies by site type and season. --Claude

was: Private RV park at the corner of Hwy 9 and North Dinosaur Trail in Drumheller, a short walk from the World's Largest Dinosaur. Full-service RV sites with 30/50-amp plus rental cabins; open seasonally. Nightly/transient bookings via Campspot ($60-73/night 2026 by service level). --Claude
note: RV park in Drumheller, in the Badlands, a short walk from the World's Largest Dinosaur, swimming and downtown, a short drive from the Royal Tyrrell Museum and 15 minutes from the Hoodoos and the Atlas Coal Mine.  Its sites are split between the East Park and the West Park, and portable fire pits are available; there is also an ATM, e-bike rental (C$75 a full day) and four lodgings, from Littlefoot Lodge to the Cabana. --Claude

was: Private campground on Hwy 9 about 17 km west of Drumheller, seconds from Horseshoe Canyon in the badlands. 48 fully-serviced RV sites (30/50-amp, water/sewer, pull-throughs for big rigs) plus deluxe and rustic cabins; washrooms/showers, store, playground. Nightly/transient bookings via Campspot. --Claude
note: Campground seconds from Horseshoe Canyon's views and hiking trails and minutes from Drumheller's attractions, with big-rig-friendly sites.  There is a playground, mini-golf, ice cream, fire pits and firewood, and deluxe and camping cabins are rented. --Claude

was: Large lakeside resort on Gull Lake near Bentley. 72 nightly/transient RV sites alongside ~550 seasonal lots (30/50-amp, full hookups; from ~$40 CAD/night), plus beach, boat launch and 18-hole golf. Open seasonally; transient sites reservable via Campspot — genuine nightly inventory beyond the seasonal section. --Claude
note: Daily-fee RV park in Sandy Point, a gated resort community of 800 acres with 4.5 km of natural lakefront on the south-western shore of Gull Lake, 10 minutes west of Highway 2 and 5 km from Bentley; it sits alongside seasonal sites and ownership lots.  Its easy back-in sites are about 100 ft long and 30 ft wide on large gravel pads, each with a view of Gull Lake, a few steps from the public beach.  The resort has an inland marina and boat launch, walking trails and a golf course opening in 2026, and pets are allowed in designated areas only. --Claude

was: Coastal private park at Cape Tormentine on the Northumberland Strait. ~41 sites (full-hookup and dry), 30-amp, store, dump station, laundry, showers; daily and seasonal rates, open ~May-Sept, reservable via Campspot. Real transient RV campground. --Claude
note: Beach campground minutes from the Confederation Bridge, a stop for those going to or coming from Prince Edward Island.  Its no-service sites are right on the water, steps from the beach, and its 3-way service sites a short walk away.  The on-site store sells groceries, household items, camping essentials, coffee and ice cream, and the beach access, public washrooms and showers serve visitors and campers through the season.  Seasonal sites have a waitlist.  The campground's signature fundraiser, the Cape Tormentine Beach Music Festival, runs from July 30 to August 2, 2026. --Claude

was: Large private beachfront park at 30 Chemin Plage Gagnon, Grand Barachois, on the Northumberland Strait. Mix of seasonal and nightly transient sites: unserviced field sites, 2-service (elec+water) and 3-service (elec/water/sewer, mostly drive-thru) RV sites; nightly transient booking via Campspot ($41-150 CAD, min 1 night). Open ~May 21 - Sep 24. --Claude
note: Campground 19 km (12 miles) east of Shediac off Highway 133, at the border of Cap-Pelé and Grand-Barachois, beside Gagnon Beach, with its sunsets, sandbars for miles and what the campground calls the warmest waters north of Virginia.  Every site is 2 to 5 minutes' walk from the sand.  There is an animal-friendly area, a playground with a bouncy pillow, a basketball court, a recreation hall for pool, ping-pong and other indoor games, a new family inground pool and a large field.  Sites run from unserviced field camping to 2-service sites in the main area (20 amps) or the open field (20 or 30 amps) and 3-service sites (30 amps), mostly drive-through.  Wi-Fi costs extra, C$7 a day per device.  The campground also rents trailers and a studio cottage, and seasonal sites have a waitlist.  Max Michaud, Pat Jacob and Fred Jacob have owned it since August 2024; it is over 40 years old.  A beach day pass or visitor pass costs C$10 a carload. --Claude

was: RV campground on the Mactaquac head pond of the Saint John River at Upper Queensbury, across from Nackawic; full-service, partially-serviced and unserviced sites incl pull-thrus, private dock, laundry, playground. Nightly transient camping bookable via Campspot; season May-Oct. --Claude
note: Campground beside the Mactaquac head pond, part of the Saint John River, across from Nackawic and the World's Largest Axe.  It has a sandy beach and docks for boating and fishing, kayak rentals, a playground, horseshoes and washer toss, and live music, barbecues and pig roasts on summer Saturdays.  Nackawic, 3 minutes away, has groceries, a liquor store, a pharmacy and a marina with a paved launch and fuel; golf is within 5 minutes, and ATV trails and Kings Landing are nearby.  Cabins and trailers are also rented.  Quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 8 a.m., and a site holds at most 10 people. --Claude

was: Private campground on the Saint John River (Mactaquac headpond) at Hawkshaw, est. 1999; 50 sites, 40 full-hookup, 50-amp pull-throughs, max length up to 75 ft. Nightly $57 (30-amp/water) to $68 (50-amp/W/S); both seasonal & transient; reservable via Campspot. Open May 1 – Oct 31. --Claude
note: Boutique-style campground overlooking the Saint John River at Hawkshaw, with optional valet parking, an adults-only section and big-rig-friendly sites.  A heated 20 x 40 ft pool, open from the May long weekend to the end of September, has poolside tiki huts and a palapa; there are lawn games, a 64-ft dock for swimming, fishing and boats, kayak and bicycle rentals, a community rec centre, a stage for special events, Level 2 EV chargers (paid) and a book and DVD exchange.  A site holds at most 6 people; day visitors pay C$5 and overnight guests C$8. --Claude

was: Commercial 41-unit beachfront campground on the Gulf of St. Lawrence at Inverness, gateway to the Cabot Trail. Serviced sites (water/electric) plus tenting, dump station, showers, laundry and general store; nightly bookings via Campspot; also rents cottages. Seasonal. --Claude
note: Cottage and campground village on the outskirts of Inverness, above the sandy shores of the Gulf of St. Lawrence between two world-class golf courses, with private beach access, ocean sunsets and the Cabot Trail at its back door; the MacLeod family has run it since 1985.  Its unserviced sites take tents, pop-ups, teardrops, truck campers and small camper vans (18 ft), but no motor homes, RVs or travel trailers, and a site can be locked.  Tents aren't allowed on RV sites.  Wi-Fi is in the cottages but not on the campsites, and ATV stays need the village's approval, 4 at most at a time.  It also has 41 housekeeping cottages. --Claude

was: Coastal park at Hunts Point on the South Shore (near Summerville Beach). About 32 sites with full 3-way service + 2 water/electric + 3 overflow + 5 tent sites; ocean/beach access across the road. Open ~May 15-Oct 15. Reservable online via Campspot. --Claude
note: William and Sandra Robinson's campground, nestled in the trees across from Hunts Point Beach, a 4-minute walk away; Summerville Beach is an 8-minute drive, Carters Beach 5 minutes past it, and Liverpool 12 km.  Sites are gravel, with a picnic table and fire pit, and two solar-powered sites suit pop-up trailers, vans or tents; three unserviced tent sites have 12 x 12 ft sand pads, and T1 also fits a car or van.  Four rental RVs, 26 to 32 ft, are on site, and so is the Cove Coffee & Snack Bar; e-bikes, hoverboards and propane fire pits are rented.  The shower house is heated, there is a kitchen area, and fresh eggs and live lobsters are sold. --Claude

season.note: The main season opens May 1 (earlier on request); winter camping by inquiry.

was: Family campground (since 1985) at 11373 Highway 4, Havre Boucher, 15 min from the Canso Causeway. 69 campsites incl pull-through RV sites with 30-amp power/water/sewer, plus tent sites and 2 ocean-view cabins; no seasonal rentals (all transient). Open ~May 16–Oct 19. Reservable online via Campspot. --Claude
note: Campground at Havre Boucher with ocean-view RV sites and, in the E section, primitive sites beside the water.  Swimming is off the dock, in what the campground calls the warmest waters north of the Carolinas; there is no sandy beach, so water shoes are recommended, and there are canoes, kayaks and pedal boats.  There is beach-side volleyball, washer toss, a playground, a small walking trail, birdwatching (more than 30 kinds seen) and a book exchange.  Two cabins and a fifth-wheel trailer are rented, there are seasonal sites, and cyclists get a special rate for one tent.  Quiet hours run from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. --Claude

was: Beachfront campground at Spencers Island on the Bay of Fundy (Minas Channel). Satellite shows a row of drive-in RV/trailer sites strung along the shingle beach. No working official website found (Facebook-only presence). --Claude
note: Campground at Spencer's Island on the Bay of Fundy, where every site has a front-row seat to the bay.  The land was a shipyard with a lighthouse, then a lumber yard; Bob and Noreen ran the campground from 1999, and Bill and Joanne have since 2023.  Lobster season runs to the end of July, a public boat ramp is right next to the campground, and there is a book exchange.  From June 27 to August 29 the cottages rent by the week only, Saturday to Saturday.  Check Cumberland County's burn restrictions before lighting a fire. --Claude

was: Small private campground in the Garrett County forest at 2,740 ft, less than a mile from New Germany State Park and its lake, swimming, fishing and boat rentals. 18 RV sites, nine tent sites and five A-frame cabins; 20/30/50-amp electric and rigs accepted to 36 ft, but NO water or sewer at the sites - there is a water filling station beside the bathhouse and a dump station on site. 2025 season rates: $38/night electric site for tent or RV, $28 primitive tent, $75 small A-frame cabin; nightly and seasonal rates both offered, open roughly March/April to December. Bathhouse with showers, general store selling firewood, wifi, 10% military and first-responder discount; also a Harvest Hosts location. Bookable on Campspot. CAVEAT on the pin: three sources disagree by up to 1.7 km on where this sits (US Census rooftop match on the operator's own published address, RV Life's pin 680 m west, Campspot's coordinates 1.7 km west) and Esri imagery is unbroken canopy at all three, so the coordinate here is the address match rather than a confirmed loop. NOT confused with New Germany State Park Campground (id 63), which is the separate state-run campground next door. RV Life 4.5*/$$ ~$39/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Small campground in the Appalachian Mountains of Garrett County, family-owned since 1964 (Grace and Doc Shunk), 2 miles from New Germany State Park.  Its rustic, shady sites are mostly back-ins on gravel, with some pull-throughs, and may need levelling; an RV water-filling station and a wash sink stand outside the renovated, heated bathhouse.  The sewer disposal area doesn't accommodate modern RVs but takes a rolling portable tank, and New Germany State Park's dump station is less than 5 miles away.  The small Glamp Store is open around the clock, fiber Wi-Fi arrived in summer 2026, and cell service is limited.  A-frame and other cabins are rented, a new pavilion is coming, and political flags aren't allowed.  CAVEAT on the pin: three sources disagree by up to 1.7 km on where this sits (a US Census rooftop match on the operator's published address, RV Life's pin 680 m west and Campspot's coordinates 1.7 km west), and Esri imagery is unbroken canopy at all three, so the coordinate here is the address match rather than a confirmed loop.  Not to be confused with New Germany State Park Campground (id 63), the separate state-run campground nearby. --Claude

was: Open-country park on SD-79 at Hermosa, 13 miles south of Rapid City and handy to Custer State Park's east entrance. 38 pull-thru sites, all full hookup at 50 or 30 amp, most taking rigs to 75 ft, plus back-ins; modern shower house, laundry, propane and free wifi. Bookable through Campspot. Priced above the sweep's usual private gate. RV Life 4.5*/$$$ (auto 9/2026)
note: Campground among ponderosa pines and rolling hills on SD-79 at Hermosa, a base for Mount Rushmore, Crazy Horse and Deadwood.  It has spacious sites, a dog park, a fire pit and propane; Dollar General and the Lazy R are within walking distance, and Corner Pantry is half a mile away.  Monthly stays are offered at a discounted rate from November 1 to April 1. --Claude

was: Family-run since 1969 (third generation) on Gordon St just south of I-196/Chicago Dr, Zeeland; full-hookup and water/electric RV sites to 50 amp, pool, fishing pond, cabins; open April-November, booked online via Campspot. Operator rates page: $48-52/night for 2 adults + 2 kids; Campspot quote for a June 2027 weeknight: W/E $49, full hookup $54. Pop-ups (rustic) limited to one week. RV Life 4*/$$$ ~$48/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Family campground opened in August 1969 in a gravel pit dug for the highway, and run by three generations of the Riemersma family.  It has a fishing pond with boat rentals, a pool (added in 1975), a rec room, an activity field, a playground and PumpkinFest, and rents cabins.  Rustic pop-up sites take stays of a week at most, holidays and Tulip Time take a 3-night minimum, and clubs are welcome. --Claude

was: Family campground on a small pond north of M-55 west of West Branch; water/electric and electric-only RV sites (20/30/50 amp), double-deluxe pull-throughs to 80 ft, beach tent sites, cabins and an RV rental; honey wagon and dump station. Operator 2025 nightly ranges: W/E 30A $45-57, electric-only 30A $38-49; Campspot June 2027 weeknight: $47. 3-night minimum on holiday weekends. RV Life 5*/$$$ ~$45/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Country campground in Ogemaw County beside a big pond stocked for catch-and-release fishing, with a swimming beach and kayaks, a canoe and paddle boats.  There is volleyball, a playground, a sharing library, basketball hoops and a community area by the pond.  Campers can ride from the campground to the ORV and snowmobile trails, and DNR ORV licences are sold.  It rents tents, sleeping bags, a 2019 VLite camper and cabins.  Clear Lake's public boat launch is a mile away, Ogemaw Nature Park just over 2 miles, and the Rifle River Recreation Area is nearby.  Storage costs $35 a month; electric-only sites can have their fresh-water tanks filled, or their holding tanks emptied by the honey wagon, for a fee, and propane is sold.  Holiday weekends take a 3-night minimum, and a site may have two dogs at most. --Claude

was: Campground in open hill country near Boyne Falls with a looped layout; standard (20/30A) and deluxe (50A) back-in and pull-through RV sites plus seasonal sites, booked on Campspot. Campspot June 2027 weeknight: standard $45, deluxe $50. RV Life 4.5*/$$$ ~$41/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Campground near Boyne Falls with a heated pool, two playgrounds and an 8-acre youth ATV park for riders 16 and younger.  There are yurts, community bonfires, a propane fill station and gasoline, a basketball court, sand volleyball and horseshoe pits, a dog park, a half-mile walking trail, a sunset lookout, a pavilion for event rentals and a zip line for children, and seasonal sites are offered. --Claude

was: Family-owned campground (formerly CampDoYaWanna Campground & Party Store, new ownership) behind the camp store on US-23 just north of Harrisville, across the road from Lake Huron and near Harrisville State Park; RV/tent sites with water and 20/30/50-amp electric (no sewer; dump station and honey wagon), camper rentals. Daily rate $45 for all sites (operator and Campspot). RV Life 5*/$$$ ~$45/night (auto 9/2026). --Claude
note: Campground across the road from Lake Huron and near Harrisville State Park, with easy access to the beach; formerly CampDoYaWanna Campground & Party Store, it is now family-owned under new ownership.  Select sites are big-rig friendly, and there are shaded sites, a honey wagon, a car wash, crafts, a playground, gaga ball, sand volleyball, horseshoes and cornhole, and three RV rentals. --Claude
